prize_parts.citation: For discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and of its active form, which made possible incretin-based treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity.

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: B019 alone, credited to Holst, Drucker and Mojsov. I hold it on the science, not on the fact that all six of us ranked it first. The chain from proglucagon processing and incretin physiology, through identification of the bioactive GLP-1 peptide, to receptor biology and drugs is unusually complete. Large randomised outcome trials have independently confirmed benefit on glycaemia, weight and cardiovascular and renal outcomes, so maturity is not in question. As a physician-scientist in autoimmunity I look for discoveries where a mechanism was shown to hold in patients. Few candidates on the shortlist meet that test as fully as this one does. A single-achievement prize is also the cleanest use of the three-person cap, because the discovery trio fills it and a second part would force one of them out. The citation should say that the physiology and the active peptide made the therapies possible. That acknowledges the long-acting analogue step without naming the drug developers or ruling on the Habener question.
statement.case_against: Attribution remains the weak point. Mojsov's priority for the active GLP-1(7-36/37) form against Habener's group cannot be verified from the supplied record, and Habener is outside the credited names. Knudsen's acylated analogues are what reached patients at scale, and a prize that honours only the discovery side can read as passing over the step that delivered the benefit. In round 1 I described her work as arguably as decisive for patients as the physiology. I still think that is a fair statement of the cost. My conclusion is that, with a cap of three, the prize should rest on the discovery of the hormone's actions and the active peptide, and drug design should be recognised in the citation wording. Long-term safety, including pregnancy and young patients, is still accumulating. Nobody has argued that this changes the core discovery.

responses.point: Linnarsson said he would keep Mojsov over Knudsen because the prize rewards discovery, would treat Knudsen as the natural replacement only if the record weakens Mojsov's claim, and would put the drug step in the framing of the citation.
responses.response: I accept that ordering, and the chair's question on Mojsov's priority needs a direct answer from me. I cannot confirm priority for the active peptide from the supplied record, and no member can. The record gives us no positive evidence that her claim fails, though. The right test is whether the committee's own review of the literature would support it, and if it did not, I would move Knudsen in rather than drop to a Holst and Drucker pair. I also correct one point. Linnarsson describes my opening proposal as including Knudsen, but the shortlist record shows that my opening proposal was Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. My Knudsen concern is a reservation about the cap and not a change of laureates. I will vote for the discovery trio.

responses.point: El-Manira said that the third place is a real choice between Mojsov and Knudsen, that the citation should say the physiology enabled the therapies, and that a Holst and Drucker pair is the fallback if Mojsov's priority cannot be supported.
responses.response: I agree that the third place is a choice and not a default. I would not go to the pair as the first fallback, because that gives up the identification of the active peptide, which is the step that turned proglucagon biology into a drug target. The sequence I would follow is Mojsov if her claim stands, Knudsen if the record weakens it, and the pair only if the committee cannot agree on either. I agree with your citation approach. It should credit the active peptide form and say that the physiology made therapies possible, so that we make no claim about the drugs themselves and rule on no priority dispute. On your point about my round-1 comment on B041, that candidate is not on the shortlist. I would not reopen it here, and my reasoning is the one you gave. Anti-TNF is clinical proof of a mechanism others had identified.

responses.point: Perlmann argued that B040 is a clean Walter and Mori pair, that its medical impact being mechanistic is a weakness only on a narrow reading of the prize, and that CAR-T deserves to rank above where Sandberg put it.
responses.response: I take the force of this and it is why B040 remains one of my two alternatives. The attribution is cleaner than for most candidates. My reservation is not that mechanism is insufficient. The unfolded protein response is a discovery whose link to disease is still mostly implied, with no therapy and with PERK and ATF6 work by Ron and Kaufman outside the credited pair, as El-Manira noted. For a second part beside B019 I would still prefer B030, because the clinical proof in refractory B-cell malignancy is replicated and direct. I would not hold B040 against a later year, and I do not think the rules require a therapy. My position is that, given a choice between two mature candidates, I give weight to the one where benefit is already shown in patients. Where I differ from Perlmann is in ranking, not in principle.

responses.point: The chair limited B024 credit to Chen and Barber, regarded cGAS-STING as early because no approved therapy has come from it, and asked whether B019 should stand alone or share the prize with a second part.
responses.response: I agree on B024, and I note that my opening included Ishikawa. On reflection, I would not keep him in a prize configuration. The trainee question cannot be settled from this record, and Chen and Barber are the stable core. The case is still early, since no STING-directed therapy is approved. On the chair's question, I would let B019 stand alone. A second part would cut B019 to two names, and I cannot find a pairing that is fair to Holst, Drucker and Mojsov and also fair to a second discovery. If the committee still wants a second part, B030 with June and Sadelain would be my choice, and Rosenberg's adoptive cell transfer is a separate achievement from CAR engineering that the committee would need to settle before then.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov's priority for the active GLP-1 peptide against Habener's group can be supported, since the supplied record cannot settle it. I would substitute Knudsen if it were weakened and not drop to a pair.
Whether the committee prefers a single achievement or a split, because any second part forces B019 below three names.
Whether B030 should be CAR engineering (June, Sadelain) or adoptive cell therapy more broadly (with Rosenberg), and how Eshhar's original chimeric-receptor concept is handled.
Long-term safety and durability of incretin therapy, including pregnancy and young patients, are still open, though they do not alter the core discovery.
statement.conflict_note: No change from round 1. My profile shows autoimmunity and rheumatology research, with co-authors Kuchroo and Sonesson, and a group-leader affiliation at Bergen. None of these is a credited name on any shortlisted ballot, and I infer no personal tie from shared institutions or topics. I see no recusal need and no member has requested one.
